belief: Family means I must put up with anything.
origins: Family loyalty is a gift, but it can be bent into a trap. Some of us were taught that family comes first no matter what, that we should never speak about problems outside the home, or that forgiving means staying in harm’s way. This teaching can keep people in verbal, emotional, financial, or physical mistreatment.
teaches: Proverbs says, “The prudent see danger and take cover, but the simple keep going and suffer the consequences.” Jesus taught, “If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately.” Paul says, “Speaking the truth in love, we will in all things grow up into Christ.” The psalmist calls us to “defend the cause of the weak and fatherless… Rescue the weak and needy.” God does not ask you to accept abuse in the name of family. Honoring family and protecting yourself can go together. If you are being harmed, safety comes first.
self_statements: Family always comes first, no matter what.
I cannot say anything about how they treat me.
If I set limits, I am betraying them.
What happens at home stays at home.
They are my family, so I have to endure it.
errors: Insisting that I must tolerate anything from family.
Believing I must either accept everything or cut everyone off.
Feeling guilty about limits and concluding they are wrong.
questions: What behavior am I putting up with that hurts me or others?
Where did I learn that loyalty means silence?
What does Scripture say about protecting the vulnerable?
What would a healthy limit look like?
Who could I trust with the truth?
truth: Honoring my family does not mean accepting harm. I can speak the truth in love, set limits, and protect myself and others. If there is danger, I should seek safe help immediately.
hw_truths: I can speak the truth in love.
Honoring family does not require accepting abuse.
Protecting the vulnerable is God’s heart.
log: Each week, write one limit you set or one truth you spoke calmly.
actions: Write specifically what happens and how it affects you.
Tell a pastor, counselor, or trusted friend what is happening.
Decide what you will and will not accept, and how to communicate it.
If you or others are in danger, call 911 or the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233.
prayer: Father, I have been told to put up with things that hurt. Give me wisdom and courage to speak the truth, to protect myself and others, and to seek help where I need it. Amen.
hw_questions: What am I putting up with?
Where did I learn silence is loyal?
Who can I trust with the truth?
name_example: Sarah can write: “The prudent take cover, and I can protect myself with God’s wisdom.”
